t: A fast, low-cost RISC-V chip with wired network and high-speed USB built in.
steps: Buy the WCH CH32V307V-EVT-R1 board from LCSC, Elecrow, or Tindie.
Install the free Arduino IDE on your computer.
Add the WCH Arduino core through the Boards Manager.
Plug the board into the USB-C port marked for the built-in WCH-LinkE programmer.
Use two jumper wires to connect the user LEDs to pins PD0 and PD1.
Open the Blink example and upload it.
Try the Zephyr blinky sample next for a second way to build programs.
meta: Open Board. From $10.80. A few stores.
